account: Researchers at the School of Social Sciences of Leeds Trinity University in England ran a randomized trial with adults who had persistent tinnitus. They recruited through online advertisements with help from the charity Tinnitus UK. Participants used Woebot, a general cognitive behavioral therapy chatbot from Woebot Health, or Tinnibot, a tinnitus-specific app, or waited for eight weeks. The authors describe Woebot as a conversational agent that uses natural language processing. Among 105 participants, Woebot users lowered depression scores on the PHQ-9 from 10.03 to 8.06 and anxiety scores on the GAD-7 from 8.82 to 7.35. The waitlist did not change. Tinnibot users improved more and were the only group with a clinically meaningful drop in tinnitus distress. The authors declare no conflicts of interest, and a grant from the Australian Academy of Technology and Engineering funded the study. Tinnitus diagnoses were self-reported, all outcomes were self-reported, and the trial was not registered in advance. The authors report that the app was withdrawn from public use in June 2025.
